subject: Pilot throughput & streaming qualification — next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@fastship.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot throughput & streaming qualification — next steps

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap focused on the performance items we agreed to validate for the pilot so the engineering teams can sign off on SLOs and capacity commitments. I captured what I heard; please correct anything I missed.

Summary of FastShip workload signals from the call (your notes + DevOps):
- Steady-state: ~60 QPS, average request ~720 tokens generated (mostly ticket summarization).
- Peak bursts: up to 380 QPS for ~45s every ~6 hours (checkout and batch-import events).
- Streaming sessions: ~12 concurrent streaming connections during peak windows (live agent assist).
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end < 350ms for interactive routes, p99 < 800ms tolerated for batch/summaries.
- Concurrency requirement: ability to service 220 concurrent non-streaming requests at p95 target.

Immediate asks we promised to follow up with:
1) A preliminary throughput sizing (tokens/sec and QPS) for both steady-state and peak that maps to a recommended Dedicated slot configuration.
2) Streaming slot/profile recommendations (NVMe-backed KV cache sizing, slot count for steady vs peak).
3) A short plan for an in-pilot canary (traffic split, fallback model variant) so FastShip has predictable fallbacks if we hit capacity ceilings.
4) A list of small telemetry items we need from FastShip (sample traces, percentiles for request length, distribution of sequence lengths).

Next steps from Redwood (proposed timeline):
- Today: I’ll send a short summary + ask for the telemetry artifacts (this email).
- EOD Friday: preliminary sizing + recommended slot types (PDF) and a CSV with per-window tokens/sec assumptions.
- Next Tues: 30-minute sync to walk through the sizing, canary plan, and procurement lead time.

Attachments: I will include a preliminary snapshot template (fastship_token_profile.xlsx) — please fill the highlighted cells with representative windows if possible. Also attaching a quick reference on our slot types.

Questions I have for you now:
A) Can the SRE team provide 48 hours of high-fidelity traces that include timestamped token counts per request?
B) For streaming, do you expect double-way streaming (agent audio + token stream) or just server->client token stream?

Happy to hop on a short follow-up if that's easier.

Thanks,
Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@fastship.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@fastship.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput & streaming qualification — next steps

Michael —

Thanks for the crisp recap. A couple clarifications below; otherwise the plan looks good.

Corrections/clarifications:
- Steady-state clarification: 60 QPS is what our UI layer emits; after pre-processing we expect ~48 calls to Redwood (some requests are batched client-side).
- Average token length: 720 is an upper median — 55% of requests are under 400 tokens; we included that stat in the sheet I uploaded to the Drive (link below).
- Streaming: server->client token stream only; audio handled separately.

Answers to your questions:
A) Yes, we can share a two-day window of traces. DevOps will send a link to a zipped CSV with per-request token counts and timestamps by EOD Thursday.
B) Streaming is unidirectional (server->client).

One constraint to note: procurement needs firm slot sizing and a monthly cost estimate to start their internal PO conversation. If you can provide a conservative cost envelope in the EOD Friday deliverable, that will keep procurement moving.

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFastShipPilot

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Ellen
Director, Product 
FastShip Logistics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot throughput & streaming qualification — next steps

Adding internal notes so we can triangulate sizing quickly:

Bench inputs we should use for conservative sizing (Ben/infra):
- Model baseline: open-llama-70B dense baseline (we'll map to quantized variant for pilot).
- Token compute: assume 0.0018 sec per token on an A100-equivalent runtime for generative pass (account for KV cache hit ratio).
- Steady-state mapping: 48 effective QPS * average 400 tokens/request -> ~19,200 tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak burst mapping: for 380 QPS (external number) assume 70% route to Redwood -> 266 eff QPS; use 720 tokens/request -> ~191,520 tokens/sec during crest.
- Streaming: each streaming slot supports ~18 concurrent streams before latency degradation in our current NVMe-backed profile.

Conservative slot recommendation (quick back-of-envelope):
- Steady: 2 large slots (64GB GPU) with autoscale headroom + 10% burst buffer.
- Peak crest handling: scale to 6 slots with burst config (fast warm-up) OR apply token admission policy + fallback to a smaller model to maintain p95 latency.

Ben, can you validate the 0.0018 sec/token estimate and the stream-per-slot number? If that's accurate we'll draft the PDF with the cost envelope and two options: (A) keep interactive latency tight with higher capacity, (B) allow more fallbacks and cost savings.

Marissa
Product, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@fastship.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 08:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot throughput & streaming qualification — next steps

Ellen —

Appreciate the quick clarifications. Attached are the documents I promised: redwood_prelim_sizing.pdf (conservative and aggressive configs), the fastship_token_profile.xlsx template we discussed (partially pre-filled with your public stats), and throughput_snapshot.csv with per-window token/sec assumptions laid out.

Highlights from the conservative config:
- Steady-state: 2 reserved large slots (estimated 22k tokens/sec sustained capacity each after accounting for KV hit ratio) — covers steady with 20% headroom.
- Peak burst crest: short-lived crest requires temporary scale to 6 slots or routing 40% of crest traffic to a quantized 8-bit variant with ~10% quality delta.
- Streaming: recommend 2 streaming-optimized slots (NVMe-backed) to sustain up to 36 concurrent streams with expected p95 <= 350ms when other load is isolated.
- Canary plan: 5% traffic split for 48 hours, automated fallback to quantized variant + region-level routing to keep availability if error rate > 2%.

Procurement note: conservative monthly cost envelope included in the PDF (three-tier view: reserved + burst + monitoring add-on).

Next sync: can we target Tue Aug 10, 09:00 PT for a 30-min walkthrough? If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include Ben to answer infra-specific questions.

Thanks — I’ll follow-up once DevOps drops the traces and we re-run the tokens/sec model with their real distribution.

Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
